notes: Portal tab icon, studio while signed in as someone, kit stock said plainly · Print sizes in millimetres, and proofs that show the cut · Office: fewer clicks on orders, invoices, approvals and imports · Floor: scans that finish the job · The ordering platform you can trust: safe sends, alerts and previews

entries.title: Portal tab icon, studio while signed in as someone, kit stock said plainly
items: Design studio → Your brand → Browser tab icon: upload a square icon for the browser tab. Without one, a square logo is used, or the brand's first letter on its colour — wide logos no longer get squeezed.
The studio preview updates live even when you also have a Sign in as session open on that portal, and says whose view you're seeing, with End that session.
Kit choices that are out of stock say Out of stock in the portal, not just greyed out.
Labels with a hint no longer push their box below the others in a row (calendar reminders, counts, receiving, bulk order edits).

entries.title: Print sizes in millimetres, and proofs that show the cut
items: Pick a print size from standard sizes — A6 to A1, Letter, Tabloid, business card, posters — or type it in inches or millimetres. Bleed has one-click 0.125 in and 3 mm.
Proofs show the cut line, the bleed that's trimmed off and the keep-text-inside line, for buyers' uploads, personalized items and the staff print job page.

entries.title: Office: fewer clicks on orders, invoices, approvals and imports
items: One Change order button on an order; Ship, Close short and Cancel confirm in a window that says exactly what happens to stock and fees.
Invoices → Drafts: tick several and Issue & send them at once, each with its own result.
Approvers can Approve or Reject straight from the email — no sign-in; links work once and last 7 days.
The portal's My orders has search and pages, with tracking numbers as links.
Import check: correct a bad cell right there and check again — no spreadsheet round-trip.

entries.title: Floor: scans that finish the job
items: Scan mode saves the line you finished when you scan the next item, and says why if it can't.
Picking: scans count up, scanning the next bin confirms the stop, and a bin isn't scanned twice in a row.
Counts: count by scanning units, and add something unexpected you find in the bin.
Receive and Move suggest where to put the item; a received pallet offers Put away now.
Packing: rates load by themselves, one Buy & print label button, box weights estimated from the products.

entries.title: The ordering platform you can trust: safe sends, alerts and previews
items: Customer → Ordering platform opens with Is it working? — last synced per stream, and what's failing in plain words. Problems (refused login, the ordering platform down, no orders polled for 30 minutes, stuck items) are emailed to your problem alert addresses.
Every send to the ordering platform goes out once — no double pushes from overlapping syncs, webhooks or double clicks.
Preview what the stock push or following the ordering platform's stock would change, per SKU, before switching it on; nothing is written.
Switching on saves a copy of the ordering platform's numbers first (download as CSV), and every send is kept in a send history.
Receiving only compares like with like, new parts become SKUs only for live clients, a failed shipment check asks a person instead of guessing, and held orders go through on their own once fixed.

entries.title: The ordering platform people you can see and choose, and no button on the portal's welcome if you'd rather
items: Design studio → Hero → Button says now says it plainly: leave it empty and the welcome has no button (like Shop the catalog) at all.
Customer → Ordering platform → People shows the people straight away — name, email, group, role, how they'll sign in — with tabs for already here, skipped, user groups and cost centres.
Don't skip them: tick a shared or inactive ordering platform login to bring it in anyway (inactive ones stay switched off), or type an email for someone without one.

entries.title: Bring a client's people in from the ordering platform
items: Customer → Ordering platform → People reads the client's ordering platform user groups, users and accounting units and brings them in: groups by name, people with their role, power buyer, group and title, and cost centres. Nothing is written to the ordering platform.

People arrive inactive with no email, so they keep ordering in the ordering platform; on moving day, Go live switches them all on and sends the invitations (single sign-on people just become active). Shared logins, people with no email and duplicates are skipped and listed.

entries.title: Problem alerts by email, clearer preview errors, portal pages behind nginx, and a tidier Users list
items: Test worlds show the address testers can actually reach — inside Docker the link no longer shows the container's own address. Test worlds → Your worlds → Not the right address? Change… sets it once (like 192.168.113.40) for every world.
Customer → Client portal → Users: a Status column (Active, Invited · not accepted, Inactive), and Manage opens a person's actions under their row instead of a line of buttons running off the side.

Portal pages and the design studio's preview no longer fail with 502 Bad Gateway behind a web server (nginx) on its default settings: the storefront's fonts are no longer all announced up front, which made its response headers too big for the server.

Problem alerts: add email addresses under Settings → Health and they hear about it when something breaks — a server error, a crashed page, or the web server refusing Amphora's answer — through your own email setup, at most once an hour per problem. Send a test alert to check.

Each alert is the actual issue, in two parts: in plain words — what went wrong (named plainly when Amphora knows it), who it happened to, which client and record, where, and what to do — then the technical detail for whoever fixes it: the exact error, the request, the error reference, the version and the trace.
The design studio explains a failed preview instead of showing a bare 502 page: which server answered, what usually fixes it, and Try again.

entries.title: The design file brings the category tree and its pictures too
items: Design studio → Design file now carries every category with its picture, description and order. Bringing it in on live puts each picture on the matching category and makes the categories live doesn't have yet — assign products to them there.

entries.title: Clients add their people through the API — invited, or inactive until switched on
items: A new Manage users permission on client API keys: the brand's own systems add people as invited (the invitation email goes now) or inactive (no email; switch them on later and the invitation goes then).
They can also change a person's role, group and status by name, and resend an invitation. The key must act as a brand admin, like the People page.

entries.title: Packaging on each client's own dieline, with their art per panel
items: In the designer, add the client's dieline (PDF or AI): the page takes its size, and it shows over the page so you can draw a box on each panel — Lid, Front, sides — for the client's art.

Clients upload art per panel, checked at that panel's size. Proofs show it against the dieline; the print file never has the lines on the art, and the print-ready PDF adds the dieline as its own page for the cutter.

entries.title: Clients put their own artwork in a box on the design — checked and placed
items: A box on a design set to They upload it now takes the client's artwork as PDF, AI, SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP — not just a picture. It's checked at the box's printed size: too low a resolution is refused with the reason, soft is placed with a note, vector is sharp at any size.
The proof shows it in its spot and the print file draws it at print resolution; the check runs again when the order is placed.
Client emailed their logo? On the print job, The client's artwork → Add or Replace artwork puts it in the box, checked the same way, and re-renders the job.

entries.title: Choose exactly what each client API key may do — and change it any time
items: Customer → Client portal → API keys: Place orders now has boxes for what an order may carry — ship to any address, choose carrier and service, rush, a ship date, personalized products. A key sending something it isn't allowed gets a clear refusal naming the box.
New: Cancel orders — a key may cancel an order before the warehouse starts on it.
Change permissions on any existing key, right in the Keys list. Keys issued before keep everything they could already do.

entries.title: Change SKU codes when a brand renumbers — stock stays put, old codes keep working
items: A live SKU's code can now change: its page → SKU code → Change…. It stays the same SKU, so stock, locations, lots and history don't move and nothing is transferred.
A whole brand at once: Customer → SKUs → Change SKU codes — paste or upload old and new codes, check every row, then change them all together. Undo puts the old codes back.

The old code keeps working everywhere: old placards and case labels scan, and packing lists, sheets, orders, inbound, the client API, the ordering platform and Shopify that still say it find the SKU. Pick and pack show “was …” for 60 days.

entries.title: The print designer stops adding fields by accident
items: Clicking a dotted line of the customer's PDF now only picks it; Make it a field (or a double-click, or Enter) turns it into a field. Clicking around the page to select or deselect never adds anything.
Your fields sit on top of the PDF's dotted lines, so clicking a field always selects it — and a line a field already covers stops showing.
Leaving the designer with unsaved changes asks first.

entries.title: The design studio saves your work as you go
items: Every change in the portal design studio is kept as your draft within a moment — the top bar shows Draft saved with the time. Close the tab and the studio reopens on your changes next time, with Start from live instead if you'd rather not.
Buyers still see only what you Publish; a half-finished design never goes live on its own.

entries.title: Move a portal design from test to live with one file
items: Design studio → Design file downloads the whole look as one file — pictures, logo and web fonts included — and brings one in on another portal or install, as unpublished changes to check before Publish.
Featured products match by SKU code and user groups by name; anything the other portal doesn't have is listed after the import.
Also on the API: GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/portal-theme/export and POST …/portal-theme/import.

entries.title: Sub-categories as big blocks, and category pictures that fit
items: A parent category shows its sub-categories as big picture blocks, the same as Shop by category on the home page — including a parent with nothing in it yet. Design studio → Catalog switches between blocks (the default), chips, or only the sidebar and menu.
Category pictures always show whole — a logo is fitted inside its block, never cropped.

entries.title: Every category level in the portal menu, and a new group stays open
items: The portal's header menu shows every level of categories under a parent, indented — not just the first. Sub-category tiles list what sits under each one, and an empty category lists its sub-categories instead of stopping at Nothing here yet.
Creating a user group keeps it open on its editor, ready for its catalog, limits and rules — no Edit click.
A test world's portal developer page (/p/…/api) loads its reference for staff previewing it or signed in as one of its people.

entries.title: Empty categories show in the portal
items: A category shows in the portal's menu before any product is in it, so a brand set up with its categories first sees the whole structure from day one. Opening an empty one says Nothing here yet.
User groups still decide: a group limited to Only these categories sees just those, everything under them, and the parents that lead to them.

entries.title: Add many SKUs to a category, and categories you can tell apart
items: Each category has a SKUs tab: In category and Not in category, with search and sortable columns. Tick SKUs (or every one the search shows) and press Add to category or Remove from category. Other categories shows where each SKU already sits.

A SKU's Categories box is now the tree: each top-level category in its own box with its sub-categories under it, so two called Sale under different parents can't be mixed up. The SKU's categories are listed above as full paths, and a Find box narrows a long list.
In the portal, People is now Users — the menu, the page and the help.
On a SKU, Customs value is now Fair market value — the declared value per unit for international shipments.
